title: Board of Water Supply opposes Bill 1
summary: On September 17, a motion passed with five ayes to tell Council Member Cook's office the board does not support Bill 1. Testifiers said the water department should keep its discretion over reviews. The bill would let the department review subdivision construction plans before water is verified, and the committee had sent it back to the Board of Water Supply for comment.

timeline.text: The Water and Infrastructure Committee's items list shows Bill 1 still pending as item WAI-21 after the board's September vote.

source.quote: BILL 1 (2026), AMENDING THE WATER AVAILABILITY POLICY ON SUBDIVISION CONSTRUCTION PLANS.

timeline.text: The motion passed with five ayes.
timeline.body: Board of Water Supply

timeline.text: A motion was made to tell Council Member Cook's office the board does not support Bill 1.
timeline.body: Board of Water Supply

timeline.text: Another testifier opposed the Bill 1 amendment, saying the water department should keep its discretion.
timeline.body: Board of Water Supply

timeline.text: Members who plan to draft a response should say so to learn the deadline.

timeline.text: A council member's letter about the board's further comments on Bill 1 will be on the next meeting's agenda.

timeline.text: Chair Cook sent the Board of Water Supply a letter asking for comments on the updated CD1 version after the committee deferred the bill on Aug. 3.

source.quote: The Council's Water and Infrastructure Committee met on August 3, 2026, and deferred action on the bill.

timeline.text: The bill goes back to the Board of Water Supply for comments before the committee takes it up again.

timeline.text: A member asked that the department be asked how it prioritizes reviews, and the chair said this was noted.

timeline.text: The chair supported sending the bill back to the Board of Water Supply for review.

timeline.text: The chief engineer for water said water supply has often been the last department to finish its review.

timeline.text: Another testifier said the bill would take away the department's choice in ordering its reviews.

timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: A Pacific Rim Land representative testified in support of the bill.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: The chair said the bill lets water supply staff review plans alongside other departments.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: The chair said developers must still show written proof of long-term water before plans are approved.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: The only item was Bill 1, 2026, about water availability rules for subdivision construction plans.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: Water Supply Director John Stufflebean sent Chair Cook a memo opposing the bill's provisions.

source.publisher: Department of Water Supply, County of Maui
source.quote: In fact, it removes DWS's ability to condition or withhold construction plan approval based on water concerns.

timeline.text: The Board of Water Supply revisited Bill 1 and voted 6–0 to draft an advisory letter asking the Council to reconsider.

source.quote: Board members said Bill 1 (2026) could limit the department's ability to ensure adequate water supplies for development; Member John Helly volunteered to draft a letter asking the County Council to reconsider the proposal.

timeline.text: The committee will work with the County's lawyers on the countywide policy plan question.

timeline.text: The chair said getting written water verification can take about three to six months, and plan review now waits for it.

timeline.text: The committee is weighing Bill 1, which would let the Department of Water Supply review subdivision construction plans before water is verified.
